  Q.1 A mass-spring-damper system has 𝑚 = 1 𝑘𝑔, 𝑏 = 6 𝑁· 𝑠/𝑚, and

      𝑘 = 9 𝑁/𝑚. Based on the characteristic equation, what type of

        response does this system exhibit?

      A) Underdamped

       B) Overdamped

       C) Critically damped

      D) Unstable

       Answer: C

       Refer to Lecture 21: Linear Control of Manipulators Slide 11

         characteristic equation 𝑚𝑠² + 𝑏𝑠 + 𝑘 = 0

                             𝑠2 + 6𝑠+ 9 = 0

       𝑏2 = 62 = 36; 4𝑚𝑘= 4 × 1 × 9 = 36;

       𝑏2 = 4𝑚𝑘; critically damped system.


  Que  For a mass-spring-damper system with 𝑚 = 4, 𝑏 = 1, 𝑘 = 1, a
  2     control law 𝑓 = −𝑘ₚ𝑥 − 𝑘ᵥẋ  is applied to achieve a critically
      damped response with desired closed-loop stiffness 𝑘′ = 16. What
        are the values of 𝑘ₚ and 𝑘ᵥ respectively?
      A) 7, 15
       B) 15,7
       C) 7,7
      D) 15,15
       Answer: D
       Refer to Lecture 21: Linear Control of Manipulators Slide 19 for
        equations:

slides.title: 𝑘′ = 𝑘+ 𝑘𝑝→16 = 1 + 𝑘𝑝→𝑘𝑝= 15
slides.text:
𝑘′ = 𝑘+ 𝑘𝑝→16 = 1 + 𝑘𝑝→𝑘𝑝= 15
                       𝑏′ = 2√𝑚𝑘′ = 2√4 × 16 = 16
                   𝑏′ = 𝑏+ 𝑘𝑣→16 = 1 + 𝑘𝑣→𝑘𝑣= 15


Q.3  What does the "Back EMF" generated by a rotating DC motor do and

       is given by which equation? (where 𝑣 = voltage; 𝑘𝑚, 𝑘𝑒 = motor
      constant; 𝑖𝑎 = armature current; 𝑟𝑎 = armature resistance;  𝜃̇𝑚=
      angular velocity; 𝑙𝑎 = armature inductance)
     A) it adds to the applied voltage; 𝑣 = 𝑘𝑚· 𝑖𝑎
     B) it opposes the applied voltage; 𝑣= 𝑘𝑒. 𝜃̇𝑚
     C) it amplifies torque; 𝑣= 𝑟𝑎. 𝑖𝑎
     D) it has no effect on the circuit; 𝑣= 𝑙𝑎. 𝑖𝑎
     Answer: B

     Refer to Lecture 22: Modeling and Control of a Single Joint Slide 6


Q.4  What "rule of thumb" is given to prevent the control system from

      exciting unmodeled structural resonances?

     A) 𝜔𝑛 ≥ 2𝜔𝑟𝑒𝑠
     B) 𝜔𝑟𝑒𝑠 ≥ 2𝜔𝑛
     C) 𝜔𝑛 = 2𝜔𝑟𝑒𝑠
     D) 𝜔𝑟𝑒𝑠 ≠ 2𝜔𝑛
     Answer: B

     Refer to Lecture 22: Modeling and Control of a Single Joint Slide 11

slides.title: Q.5  What  is the purpose of a "linearizing control law" in nonlinear
slides.text:
Q.5  What  is the purpose of a "linearizing control law" in nonlinear

      control?

     A) To add more nonlinearity to the system for robustness

     B) To use a control input that cancels nonlinear effects, so the closed-

      loop system behaves in a simpler way

     C) To eliminate the need for feedback entirely

     D) No change in system dynamic model needed.

     Answer: B

     Refer to Lecture 23: Nonlinear and Time-Varying Systems Slide 8


Q.6  Compare a linear spring 𝑓1 (with constant 𝑘1) and a nonlinear spring
      𝑓2 = 𝑘2𝑥³ (with constant 𝑘2) both with coefficient value 10 (𝑘1 =
     10 𝑁/𝑚, 𝑘2 = 10 𝑁/𝑚³). At a displacement of 𝑥 = 2 m, what is the
       ratio of the nonlinear spring force to the linear spring force?

     Answer: 4

     Answer: 4

      Linear force, 𝑓1 = 𝑘1. 𝑥= 10 × 2 = 20 𝑁.
     Nonlinear force, 𝑓2 = 𝑘2. 𝑥³ = 10 × 2³ = 10 × 8 = 80 𝑁.

               𝑓2   80      Ratio,  =  = 4.
               𝑓1   20

     A) 𝛼 = 𝑀(𝜃), 𝛽 = 0

     B) 𝛼 = 0, 𝛽 = 𝐺(𝜃)

Q.8  For a single joint, the closed-loop error dynamics are given by

           𝑒̈ + 𝑘𝑣· 𝑒̇ + 𝑘𝑝· 𝑒 = 0. If 𝑘𝑣 = 6 and 𝑘𝑝 = 9,  the value of

     damping ratio (𝜁) is ___________.

     Answer: 1

     Answer: 1

     Comparing with 𝑠² + 2𝜁𝜔𝑛· 𝑠 + 𝜔𝑛² = 0:
                              𝜔𝑛2 = 9 → 𝜔𝑛 = 3;

                2𝜁𝜔𝑛 = 6 → 𝜁 = 6/(2 × 3) = 1


Q.9  In traditional joint-based control systems, errors were computed in

     which quantities?

     A) End-effector position, velocity, and force

     B) Joint position, joint velocity, and joint acceleration

     C) Cartesian force and moment only

     D) Only joint position

     Answer: B

     Refer to Lecture 25: Cartesian-Based Control Systems and Examples

      Slide 4

slides.title: Q.10  In the Transpose-Jacobian Cartesian Controller, how is the virtual
slides.text:
Q.10  In the Transpose-Jacobian Cartesian Controller, how is the virtual

      Cartesian force 𝐹 converted into joint torques?

     A) 𝜏= 𝐽−1𝐹

     B) 𝜏= 𝐹𝐽

     C) 𝜏= 𝐽𝑇𝐹

     D) 𝜏= 𝐹/𝐽

     Answer: C

      Refer to Lecture 25: Cartesian-Based Control Systems and Examples

      Slide 11





                    ***END****
